text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated error rate and latency for cross-region requests originating in eu-west-1. Symptoms: 502s and timeouts between eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 paths. Autoscale triggers suppressed. Generated at 2025-10-24T14:23:10Z

nora_oncall: I'm paged, looking. assigning to netops for routing check. pinging @jamie_netops

jamie_netops: saw the spike in the routing metrics. There was a routing policy tweak pushed ~14:20 UTC to bias latency-based routing weights for eu clusters. Rolling change details: `rbw route-policy apply --id=latency-balance-3 --workspace=prod`

maria_dev: customers reporting long response times in EU dashboards, some with 10-20s tail latencies. cs reported 8 customers affected (mostly EU SaaS tenants).

sam_sre: can we confirm whether traffic is being misrouted to us-east-1 instead of eu-west-1? quick check: `curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.example/health -o /dev/null | grep X-Routed-Region`

maria_dev: sample from eu node:
```
HTTP/2 504
X-Routed-Region: us-east-1
Server: redwood-edge
```
shows routed region wrong.

kai_infra: running traceroute from eu-edge-12:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (52.10.23.45), 30 hops max
 1  10.1.2.1 (10.1.2.1)  0.49 ms
 2  upstream-pe (198.51.100.1)  3.2 ms
 3  ??? (203.0.113.5)  180.6 ms  <-- long hop to us-east
```
Looks like policy directed requests across regions.

jamie_netops: I can reproduce via the routing simulator. The policy weight for eu-west-1 was inadvertently set to 0 during the tweak, so latency-based routing falls back to us-east-1 for many prefixes. Suspect bug in `route-policy` CLI where a defaulting logic converted missing weight -> 0.

sam_sre: impact classification?

oliver_cs: Customers: 8 with visible errors, 3 with alerts firing. Severity set to P1 for now due to cross-region hard failures for EU paying tenants. Notifying account teams.

nora_oncall: mitigation options: 1) pin region for api.* to eu-west-1 (fast, manual) 2) rollback policy change (needs deploy) 3) add emergency override route with higher priority. Which do we want?

jamie_netops: I recommend pin-region for immediate relief, then rollback the faulty policy. I'll push the override and publish change.

nora_oncall: ok do it. @jamie_netops, execute and post the exact command. keep deploy-bot ready for rollback.

jamie_netops: running:
```
rbw route-manager pin-region --service "api" --from-region eu-west-1 --to-region eu-west-1 --duration 30m --reason "emergency pin to mitigate policy bug"
```
Applying... done.

deploy-bot: :inbox_tray: CONFIG CHANGE: route-manager pin-region applied by jamie_netops (change-id: ch_20251024_1428).

sam_sre: verifying...
```
curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.example/health -o /dev/null | grep X-Routed-Region
X-Routed-Region: eu-west-1
```
latencies back to normal for sampled probes: p50 42ms, p95 110ms.

maria_dev: customers reporting recovery. alerts clearing. :thumbsup:

nora_oncall: marking mitigation in incident timeline. Next: rollback the buggy policy and run unit test for CLI defaulting. Who will own rollback?

jamie_netops: I'll prepare rollback PR and coordinate the deploy. target: 14:45 UTC. Will also add a predeploy check that rejects empty weight fields.

kai_infra: handover to infra for deeper analysis and postmortem. @nora_oncall handing to @kai_infra for follow-up and root cause.

nora_oncall: handing over. I've updated the incident: impact P1 -> mitigated (routing pinned). Please document timeline.

oliver_cs: I've emailed affected customers with an interim note. Will follow-up after RCA.

kai_infra: quick notes: initial root cause appears to be policy-engine treating missing `weight` as 0 when building the latency-balancing table. We should audit policy change tools for schema validation. Also check whether the change broadcast to edge config had any transient replication lag.

sam_sre: logs to attach for postmortem: router-proxyd logs around 14:20-14:30 (error bursts), route-api audit trail for policy change id `latency-balance-3` and event that removed weight. I'll save and link to the incident doc.

jamie_netops: rollback done at 14:46 UTC: `rbw route-policy apply --id=latency-balance-3 --from-file=latency-balance-3.rollback.yaml` deploy-bot confirmed.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: DEPLOY OK: rollback applied by jamie_netops (deploy-id: d_20251024_1446).

sam_sre: re-verification:
```
curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.example/health -o /dev/null | grep X-Routed-Region
X-Routed-Region: eu-west-1
```
No errors observed in 15m rolling window.

nora_oncall: closing the active page. Handing final ownership to @kai_infra for RCA and action items.

kai_infra: action items assigned:
- jamie_netops: add validation to route-policy CLI (reject empty weights) and write unit tests
- sam_sre: add canary probes to detect region pin regressions faster (deploy metric alert)
- infra: audit config replication and add a checksum check on edge nodes
- cs: follow-up comms to customers with timeline and fixes

oliver_cs: will coordinate customer messaging.

jamie_netops: ETA for fixes: validation PR in 24h, unit tests same day, deploy next week in low-traffic window.

nora_oncall: thanks all. Incident resolved and mitigated. Will create incident ticket and calendar postmortem. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident archived (incident_id: INC-2025-1024-47)."
